name: Upper-Arm-Pad Chest Fly
definition: A seated fixed-path shoulder-horizontal-adduction isolation on the exact Life Fitness Pro 2 PSPEC fixture. Both elbows and forearms remain comfortably against the lever pads while the athlete grips and rotates the handles and brings the elbows toward one another. This combined pad-and-handle joint interface differs from the handled-only chest-fly contract, so the exact fixture owns a separate family without claiming that the pads eliminate hand loading. Handled-only machines, free weights, cables, bands, pressing, rear-delt use, and other pec-deck topologies remain outside it.

exercises.name: Life Fitness Pro 2 Upper-Arm-Pad Pec Fly

execution.startingPosition: Compare the entered load only on this Life Fitness Pro 2 PSPEC fixture. Sit against the back pad, choose a comfortable start, keep both elbows slightly below shoulder height, and keep both elbows and forearms comfortably against the pads while gripping the handles.
execution.movement: Grip and rotate both handles while bringing the elbows toward one another through the guided lever path and keeping the forearms on the pads.
execution.endpoint: Stop when the elbows meet or reach the machine's comfortable closed position.
execution.returnPhase: Open both lever arms together under control to the selected start position.
execution.controlledJoints: Create the repetition by bringing both upper arms inward while holding the elbow angle and maintaining the combined pad-and-handle contact.
execution.supportAndPosture: Keep the torso against the posterior pad and the lower body still.
disqualifyingCompensations: Letting either elbow or forearm leave its pad changes the reviewed combined pad-and-handle interface.
Lifting the torso from the back pad adds body momentum.
Moving one lever before the other leaves the simultaneous two-arm fixture.
